questions.q: What is Amazon EMR, at its core?
options: A managed cluster service for open-source big data frameworks like Spark and Hadoop, giving you control over the underlying compute
A fully serverless ETL service with no underlying cluster at all
A managed relational database engine
A CDN for distributing static data files
questions.explain: EMR provisions and manages actual EC2-based clusters running Spark, Hadoop, and related frameworks — you control the cluster rather than it being abstracted away as it is with Glue.

questions.q: You need to scale an EMR cluster's compute up temporarily for a large job, then scale back down. Should you add more core nodes or more task nodes, and why?
options: Task nodes — they run compute only, with no HDFS storage, so they can be added and removed freely without any data-loss risk
Core nodes — they're always cheaper to add temporarily
Either is identical in every respect
Neither — cluster size can never change after creation
questions.explain: Task nodes hold no HDFS data, so scaling them up and down is safe; removing a core node risks losing whatever HDFS data was stored on it.

questions.q: What role does the master node play in an EMR cluster?
options: It manages the cluster, running YARN's ResourceManager and tracking the health of other nodes
It only stores HDFS data and does no coordination
It is optional and most clusters run without one
It exists purely to run Spark executors
questions.explain: The master node is the cluster's coordinator — every cluster has one (or a small HA set in newer configurations) running YARN's ResourceManager and tracking node health.

questions.q: What does EMRFS let a Spark or Hadoop job running on an EMR cluster do?
options: Read and write S3 directly, rather than being limited to HDFS
Replace the need for a master node
Automatically convert Parquet files to CSV
Bypass IAM permissions entirely
questions.explain: EMRFS is EMR's S3 connector, letting jobs treat S3 as a filesystem directly rather than only working against the cluster's own HDFS storage.

questions.q: Which node type in EMR stores data via HDFS in addition to running tasks?
options: Core nodes
Task nodes
Master nodes only
None — EMR never uses HDFS
questions.explain: Core nodes both run tasks and hold HDFS data, which is why removing one carries data-loss risk in a way that removing a task node does not.
